turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I’m here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it really should. Just... just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture this really bad turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight. I mean, logically I know people fly safely every single day, but I just can't seem to shake it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient reports marked fear of flying that is recognized as disproportionate to the actual danger ('way scarier than it really should', knowing logically that people fly safely).

turns.doctor_question: Is it just flying that makes you feel anxious, or are there other situations that trigger similar feelings of fear?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just flying. I mean, I don't have any problems with elevators, or heights, or anything else like that. It's just getting on an airplane that really gets to me.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms that flying specifically causes her fear and anxiety ('really just flying', 'getting on an airplane that really gets to me').

turns.doctor_question: Has your fear of flying stopped you from taking flights or significantly affected your travel plans?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it really has. Lately I’ve been choosing to just take long drives instead, or I'll even turn down work trainings if it means I have to fly. And if I absolutely have to talk about taking a trip, I need my husband sitting right there with me just to get through it without backing out.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly confirms actively avoiding flying by taking long drives, turning down work trainings, and needing her husband present as support to discuss travel plans.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a panic attack, either on a plane or in another situation?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't. I mean, I get really anxious and my heart races when I think about flying or when I'm on a plane, but I've never had a full-blown panic attack. It's just a really strong fear, not like I'm losing control or anything.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes experiencing a 'really strong fear' and anxiety specifically related to flying.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient describes immediate physiological fear responses (heart racing) and anticipatory anxiety when on a plane or thinking about flying.

turns.doctor_question: Is your fear more about the act of flying itself, like crashing, or is it about being in the airplane environment?
turns.patient_response: I guess I'm not totally sure. I haven't really separated the two in my head. I just know the whole idea of getting on the plane and being up in the air is what scares me. I don't really know if it's the crashing part or just being stuck in there. It's just the whole thing.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient expresses a marked fear of flying, stating that 'the whole idea of getting on the plane and being up in the air is what scares me.'

turns.doctor_question: Is your fear of flying more related to the loss of control you might feel when you're on a plane?
turns.patient_response: I don't think it's about losing control, really. I mean, I'm not sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just know that being on the plane is what makes me so anxious.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms experiencing marked anxiety specifically associated with being on an airplane, indicating a situational specific phobia.

turns.doctor_question: Is your fear of flying more about the possibility of the plane crashing?
turns.patient_response: I'm really not sure. I mean, obviously nobody wants to crash, but I don't think I'm sitting there constantly picturing the plane going down. It's just... the whole situation of being up there that makes me anxious, rather than just that one specific thought.

turns.doctor_question: Is there something specific that happens when you're on a plane, like takeoff or landing, that makes you more anxious than other parts of the flight?
turns.patient_response: I don't think so. I haven't really noticed one part being worse than another. Whether it's taking off, landing, or just sitting there in the middle of the flight... it all just feels the same to me. It's just a general feeling of being anxious the whole time.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying focused on the thought of being in a confined space?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say it's that. I don't really have a problem with small spaces or feeling closed in when I'm anywhere else. It's really just the act of being on the plane itself, not necessarily the size of the cabin.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying more related to the thought of something bad happening during the flight?
turns.patient_response: I don't think so. I mean, I'm not sitting there waiting for the engine to blow up or anything. It's just... I don't know, it's just the whole experience of flying that makes me feel on edge. I can't really pinpoint one specific bad thing I'm worried about happening.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the thought of not being able to escape if something goes wrong?
turns.patient_response: No, it's not really about escaping either. I mean, I know I can't just walk out the door when we're up in the air, but that's not what I'm focused on. It's just the flying itself.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the thought of being high above the ground?
turns.patient_response: No, it's not the height either. I'm fine looking out of tall buildings or being on balconies. It really is just... being on an airplane. I don't know why, it's just flying that does it to me.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient affirms that their anxiety is specifically triggered by being on an airplane and flying itself, consistent with a situational specific phobia.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the sensation of the plane moving or the feeling of being airborne?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I mean, I don't get motion sickness or feel weird when the plane is actually moving or taking off. It's just... the whole situation. I wish I could give you a more specific reason, but I really just don't know what exact part of it sets me off. It's just being on the plane.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the thought of not being in control of your surroundings during the flight?
turns.patient_response: No, it's not really a control thing either. I mean, I'm used to not being in control of everything, especially working at a school, so that doesn't really bother me. I just... I don't know. I really don't have a good reason for it. It's just the flying.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the thought of something going wrong with the plane itself?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really think about the mechanics of it or worry about the plane crashing or anything like that. It's not a fear of an accident. I know flying is safe. Like I said, it's just the actual act of being on the plane that makes me anxious, and I really can't pinpoint why.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms experiencing anxiety specifically triggered by being on a plane despite acknowledging that flying is safe, which aligns with situational specific phobia.

turns.doctor_question: Is your anxiety about flying related to the thought of being on the plane with other people?
turns.patient_response: No, it's not the other people either. I'm around people all day at the school, so crowds or strangers don't bother me at all. I really wish I could give you a specific reason, but it's just none of those things. It's just the flying itself.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think you would feel anxious if you were on a plane but not actually flying, like if it was parked at the gate?
turns.patient_response: I've never really thought about that. I guess... no, probably not? If it's just sitting there on the ground and not moving, I don't think that would bother me. It's the actual being up in the air part that gets to me.

turns.doctor_question: Would you feel anxious if you were in a flight simulator that felt exactly like a real plane but wasn't actually flying?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I've never been in one of those. I guess... if I knew I was actually just on the ground in a building, maybe I'd be fine? But if it really, truly felt like we were up in the air, it might still bother me. I just don't know since I haven't ever tried it.

turns.doctor_question: Would your anxiety about flying change if you were flying for a very positive or exciting reason, like a honeymoon or a dream vacation?
turns.patient_response: I don't think it would make much of a difference. I mean, I'd be really excited about the trip itself, obviously, but... I still have to actually get on the plane and be up in the air. So, no, I think the anxiety about the flying part would probably be exactly the same, no matter where I was going or why.

turns.doctor_question: Would you feel anxious if you were in a situation that felt exactly like flying, but wasn't actually flying and you were still on the ground?
turns.patient_response:
I think that's pretty much like the simulator thing you just mentioned. I really don't know. Since I've never been in a situation like that, it's hard to say for sure. 

If it felt exactly like we were in the air, maybe I'd get a little nervous? But knowing I'm actually on the ground might make it okay. I'm honestly just guessing, though, since I haven't ever experienced anything like that.
